# Set 43 candidate Saturday entry intake — proposed exact contract

Status: **draft for root and independent review**, November 17, 2026. Source baseline: chain commit `81ef2816b42b9a10f0a37da90c5a967c7a93330b` and its existing desktop workspace. This document proposes engineering bytes and behavior; it does not authorize implementation, oracle generation, official league operation, or deployment. No new product decision is inferred. Set 42 package/deployment evidence remains separate.

## 1. Outcome, authority and deliberate boundary

In the existing Candidate Pilot, an authenticated owner explicitly saves, replaces or withdraws up to five rostered, nonretired candidate fighters for a named Saturday, with at most one per weight class and no fee. A saved entry survives logout/restart, is reconciled after an uncertain reply, and remains queryable when the calendar advances. Intake closes at the exact compiled Saturday-noon Pacific cutoff. The only post-cutoff event phase is `closed_pending_lock`.

Settled sources: spec §7 D29/D34/D45, §10 D21–23/D43/D68, §11 D26/D27, §12 D72, §17 D74 and publication-format engineering delegation. See `BRAWLCHAIN_SPEC.md:68`, `:70`, `:76`, `:103`, `:115`, `:135`, `:182`, `:189`; `BUILD_PLAN.md:299`; `LAUNCH_READINESS.md:128`. D65/D75, condition v1, compiled fixture identities, stable assignments, existing receipts, all wallet paths and old previews remain unchanged.

This is a candidate intake authority borrowing an existing trusted assignment/roster authority. It is not transferable ownership, an official league admission, a booked bout, a locked card, an entropy commitment, a fee payment, a results/points ledger, or training/XP. No API in this version can set `locked`, select a block, create a seed, pair fighters, award anything, or alter the roster. No caller-supplied receipt, manifest, condition, timestamp or eligibility boolean is authoritative input.

The reusable core is new package `gymentry`, with one store per personal gym. Each store borrows one concrete `*gymstable.Store`; the stable store in turn borrows its exact manifest authority. The two published fixture gyms in one local account root share an event namespace and calendar, but retain separate entry histories. This local namespace is account-authority-specific: it is not globally unique across providers, an official event authority, or portable accepted ownership. A future official activation cannot relabel these saved candidate entries as official history. The core has no HTTP service, public registration, discovery, import or ownership-transfer endpoint.

## 2. Calendar and identities

### 2.1 Frozen calendar input

Calendar version 1 uses only the exact **1,294-byte TZif2** member `America/Los_Angeles` from `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/go/1.27.4/libexec/lib/time/zoneinfo.zip`. Member SHA256 is `200d05754f6d83a371cf408d7085125797657b3b0bebeba1e508cffe86a3e5c8`; archive SHA256 is `b2d18a7c8fa8142097a48c99609fb3c92db5ee98bc740294e57eab8ae9f94779`. Implementation must retain and embed those member bytes, verify the pin, and use `time.LoadLocationFromTZData`. Host timezone, `TZ`, installed tzdata updates and local-browser conversion never change authority results. This pins a candidate calendar interpretation, not a promise that future civil-time law cannot change.

Supported event dates are canonical ASCII `YYYY-MM-DD`, Gregorian years **2026 through 2099 inclusive**, exactly ten bytes, valid dates and Saturdays. Cutoff is local 12:00:00.000 on that date under the pinned location, converted to positive UTC Unix milliseconds. Conversion must round-trip to the identical local date/time; no normalization of impossible dates. Outside the supported date range fails `entry_calendar`; never extrapolate with the host calendar. A later calendar/rules version must produce different IDs and preserve old event bytes.

There is no new entry-opening restriction: an explicitly selected supported future Saturday may be entered before its cutoff, subject to storage quotas. A default “Upcoming Saturday” selector chooses the earliest supported Saturday with `cutoff_ms > authoritative_now_ms`; at equality it chooses the following Saturday. This is navigation only. It never retargets an existing request, pending operation, selected event or receipt. Old events remain available through history and exact-ID lookup. Merely displaying the next date never enters a fighter or allocates all intervening events.

### 2.2 Exact preimages

`H` is SHA256, rendered as 64 lowercase hex characters. `raw32` decodes the displayed canonical hex bytes without reversing them. `LE32`/`LE64` encode unsigned integers little-endian. `LP(s)` is `LE32(len(UTF8(s))) || UTF8(s)`. Every displayed `\0` below is one zero byte. No optional terminators or newlines are included.

- `CalendarID = H("SLUG candidate entry calendar\0v1\0" || LE32(1) || LP("America/Los_Angeles") || raw32(TZifSHA256) || LE32(2026) || LE32(2099) || LE32(6) || LE32(12) || LE32(0))`. Weekday 6 means Saturday with Sunday 0; the final values mean hour 12 and minute 0, with seconds/milliseconds fixed zero.
- `RulesID = H("SLUG candidate entry rules\0v1\0" || LE32(1) || LE32(5) || LE32(1) || LE64(0) || LE32(1) || LE32(1) || LE32(1) || LP(fightercondition.ProjectorID) || LE32(0) || LP("light") || LP("welter") || LP("middle") || LP("light_heavy") || LP("heavy") || LP("intake-only"))`. Values mean version, gym limit, class limit, fee units, roster-required, nonretired-required, condition version, projector ID, and trusted XP=0. Those exact class spellings are the current `fightermanifest.classForWeight` enum; display labels may expand them without changing wire bytes.
- `NamespaceID = H("SLUG local candidate entry namespace\0v1\0" || LE32(network) || raw32(genesis) || raw32(account_authority_id))`.
- `StoreID = H("SLUG candidate entry store\0v1\0" || canonicalJSON(Pin))`.
- `EventID = H("SLUG candidate Saturday event\0v1\0" || raw32(namespace_id) || raw32(calendar_id) || raw32(rules_id) || ASCII(saturday) || LE64(cutoff_ms))`.
- `EntryID = H("SLUG candidate Saturday entry\0v1\0" || raw32(store_id) || raw32(event_id) || raw32(gym_id))`.
- `ReceiptDigest = H("SLUG candidate entry receipt\0v1\0" || canonicalJSON(Receipt))`.

Operation IDs are 32 random bytes from `crypto/rand`, encoded lowercase hex, generated inside the authority. Try at most eight collisions against retained operation IDs; fail closed afterward. They are public idempotency handles, not credentials. Neither tokens nor keys enter a preimage or journal. Generation/view bind an operation, never `StoreID`, `EventID` or `EntryID`.

## 3. Core shapes and canonical encoding

The following field order is normative for each JSON object. Names are literal snake_case. All fields appear, including zero values and empty strings; arrays are `[]`, never null. Only the explicitly nullable pointers below permit null. Unknown/duplicate decoded keys, wrong scalar types, invalid UTF-8, BOM, trailing values and noninteger number spellings fail before DTO allocation. Canonical storage uses no whitespace, HTML escapes, exponent/fraction/negative integer spelling or omitted fields; a marker alone adds exactly one trailing LF. Transport may contain JSON whitespace/order differences and escaped ASCII key spelling, then must normalize through the same typed validator before canonical encoding. Duplicate *decoded* keys always fail.

Except constants, integers are bounded to JavaScript-safe nonnegative integers; timestamps are positive and at most 8,640,000,000,000,000, with explicitly documented zero sentinels. IDs are exact lowercase hex; request strings do not accept uppercase, prefixes or surrounding whitespace. Arrays of requested fighter IDs are strictly ascending by canonical prospect ID, unique and at most five; callers may sort their own selection before constructing the request. No floats occur anywhere in entry DTOs. The sole signed nested integer exception is `CheckMember.item.manifest.portrait.shoulder_jitter`, exactly -6..6 under its existing manifest validator; it uses canonical signed decimal (never -0). No generic permission for negative integers follows.

`Pin`: `version=1, namespace_id, calendar_id, rules_id, stable_store_id, stable_pin`. `stable_pin` is the exact existing `gymstable.Pin`, including account authority/account, complete published-fixture identity, concrete manifest authority pin and condition selector. `stable_store_id` must equal the existing `gymstable.ID(stable_pin)`. Every computed ID above must match; only compiled candidate selectors and the current two published fixture identities resolve. `ValidatePin` is structural+compiled-candidate validation, not a public trust-discovery API.

`Event`: `version=1, event_id, namespace_id, calendar_id, rules_id, saturday, cutoff_ms`. It is fully deterministic from Pin+Saturday. It has no seed, block, title/undercard flag or dynamic phase.

`Request`: `version=1, event_id, saturday, action, expected_revision, expected_roster_revision, prospect_ids`. `action` is `replace` or `withdraw`. Replace has 1..5 IDs and a concrete expected roster revision (zero is valid for the initial empty roster, though no successful nonempty selection is possible then). Withdraw has `prospect_ids=[]` and `expected_roster_revision=0`; it does not depend on the current roster revision or fighter eligibility. `event_id` must recompute from `saturday`, never become an opaque attacker-selected namespace.

`Intent`: `version=1, sequence, operation_id, generation, view_id, request, prepared_at_ms`. Sequence is contiguous 1..4096 across this store; generation is 1..MaxSafeInteger; prepared time is strictly before that Event's cutoff.

`Member`: `slot, assignment, class, condition_at_save`. Slot is 1..10. Assignment is the exact existing complete `gymstable.Assignment`, including canonical source-record digest. Class is from the verified manifest. Condition is exact `fightercondition.Snapshot` v1 for immutable DNA/birth, final commit time, XP=0. Members are sorted by prospect ID and agree with `Request.prospect_ids`; classes and slots are distinct. The journal retains no full source receipt, manifest, SVG, private key, login token, training or XP update.

`Receipt`: `version=1, store_id, entry_id, event, operation_id, operation_sequence, generation, view_id, action, previous_revision, revision, roster_revision, stable_checkpoint, observed_source_count, committed_at_ms, members`. Replace has 1..5 Members; withdraw has none and `roster_revision=0`. The stable checkpoint/count still record the last validated source high waters, not newly fabricated provenance. `revision = previous_revision + 1`, bounded by operation count, for **every new committed operation**, including an explicitly repeated identical selection or withdrawal of an empty entry. Idempotent replay of the *same operation* returns the identical receipt, including time/revision. This removes ambiguous no-op refresh semantics: a new acknowledged save is a new revision; a retry is not.

`Operation`: `version=1, intent, state, receipt, abandoned_at_ms`. State is `prepared`, `committed` or `abandoned`. Receipt is nonnull only when committed; abandoned time is positive only when abandoned. A committed receipt matches the entire retained intent and Event/Pin, and its time lies in `[prepared_at_ms, cutoff_ms)`. Abandon may occur at/after cutoff and under a newer authorized view; it is not an entry withdrawal. No operation can transition from one terminal state to another.

`MutationResult`: `version=1, receipt, replayed`. `OperationResult`: `version=1, store_id, operation` with operation nullable only for the explicit Pending query when absent; exact-ID lookup absence is `entry_not_found`.

`EventStatus`: `version=1, store_id, event, exists, phase, entry_id, revision, latest_operation_id, latest_receipt_digest, saved_ids, saved_at_ms, saved_roster_revision, current_roster_revision, roster_changed, eligibility, pending_operation_id, observed_at_ms, closed_observed_at_ms`. Phase is `accepting` or `closed_pending_lock`; `eligibility` is always `not_checked` for this cheap DTO. `saved_ids=[]` for never saved or withdrawn; revision distinguishes them. `pending_operation_id` here is event-scoped: it is the one pending ID only if its Request names this Event, otherwise empty. EntrySnapshot separately exposes the store-global pending ID. A nonexistent event has zero revision, empty latest IDs/digest, saved time/revision zero and closed-observed zero; EntryID remains deterministic. Status may describe a nonexistent past event as closed_pending_lock without creating a row; only the store clock is retained. History enumerates existing rows only. An existing closed event has `closed_observed_at_ms >= cutoff_ms`. A saved nonempty entry with differing saved/current roster revisions sets `roster_changed=true`; this is a conservative revalidation warning, not automatic cancellation. Empty entries set it false. `observed_at_ms` is trusted fresh metadata time, never a claim of proof verification.

`CheckMember`: `slot, item, eligibility`. `item` is existing public `gymstable.Item` without its private receipt. Slot is current 0..10 (zero means off roster), eligibility is `eligible`, `not_rostered` or `retired`, with retirement taking precedence if both apply. `CheckResult`: `version=1, status, as_of_ms, roster_revision, members`. It describes the saved latest selection only, at one common source-verified as-of, and fences the entry revision/current operation as well as the captured stable revision so a concurrent entry replacement cannot mix results. Members remain sorted and at most five. An empty entry yields an empty result without proof work. It never rewrites the saved receipt, sets lock eligibility, or changes entry revision.

`HistoryPage`: `version=1, store_id, after_event_id, next_event_id, has_more, observed_at_ms, events`. At most eight EventStatus objects, ordered by `(cutoff_ms,event_id)`; nonempty `after_event_id` must name a retained row, not be interpreted as a raw byte ordering cursor. Existing history never disappears when Upcoming changes.

Proposed fixed limits: entry-store marker 8 KiB; metadata 8 KiB; Event row 2 KiB; Operation row 32 KiB; request 8 KiB; public response 128 KiB; Member 4 KiB; public CheckMember 10 KiB; max retained events 256, operations 4096, one unresolved prepared operation per gym store, history page 8, selected IDs 5. Strict object depth is at most 10; key names at most 64 bytes. Only known arrays at declared paths are permitted: selection/saved IDs/members <=5, history events <=8, nested immutable stable slots exactly10 if a future typed wrapper includes a Status (this contract's core DTOs do not). Before freeze, independent maximum-shape calculation must confirm these caps for current nested Assignment/Condition/Item types; no silent cap increase during implementation.

## 4. Borrowed source, authorization and lock order

Add `gymaccount.EntryManage = "entry-manage"` to the existing capability allowlist. It requires a current enrolled login session; mining tokens fail. It is not one of D72's enumerated held capabilities: a newly authorized held session may save/replace/withdraw/abandon candidate entries. No fresh-auth restriction is invented. Account reset revokes original sessions immediately. Re-login at the same generation still has a new view and cannot apply an old prepared intent. Reading current/historical entries uses View; all intentional mutations use EntryManage.

`gymentry.Session` is the existing trusted `gymstable.Session` shape, passed by the captured account wrapper, never parsed from a public body. Entry core validates the exact account/enrollment against Pin during every original-session lease. `accountpilot.withCapability` applies the existing RosterManage-only signed_in-and-not-operation guard equally to EntryManage; a signing-in/resetting parent is not permitted to publish an entry mutation. The entry constructor borrows the concrete stable store; it never owns or closes it. Every entry operation drains before stable Close/rebind, which drains before manifest authority Close. No public rebind setter exists: close/reopen the entry handle with the exact validated new borrowed handle during the existing lane's source lifecycle transition.

Three narrow additive stable APIs are proposed:

1. `EntrySourceInfo(ctx) (EntrySourceInfo, error)` returns owned public `{version,store_id,pin,checkpoint,observed_source_count,roster_revision}` under its gate, with no proof, account token, roster IDs or claim of authenticated entry eligibility. It checks state/metadata and never initializes, catches up, calls registry.Info or verifies proofs. It reports the stable store's already retained observations, not an independently current manifest source count. This lets constructors bind the *actual borrowed source*, rather than trust a caller-supplied Status.
2. `ReadEntrySelection(ctx, session, ids []string) (EntrySelection, error)` uses View, fully verifies <=5 consumed source records serially, checks exact retained assignments/source-record digests, captures current slots and one common as-of, and publishes under the original View lease with final source checkpoint/roster revision fences. Returns `{version,status,as_of_ms,members:[{slot,item}]}`; off-roster and retired are represented for read-only warnings. It does not catch up missing assignments.
3. `WithEntrySelection(ctx, session, expectedRosterRevision, ids, fn func(EntrySelection, func() error) error) error` uses EntryManage and the same bounded verification, then holds the original account lease and short stable mutex across a single synchronous trusted callback. It verifies expected revision both before proofs and at final publication, retained assignment equality, source identity and final condition. The callback receives no caller-supplied records. All stable clock/observation writes must succeed **before** invoking the callback; no stable write follows it. A callback may take the entry mutex and perform one bounded entry batch, but must not reenter source, stable, account or helper controllers. Check callback runs synchronously once; its error and outer lease error cannot be swallowed.

Global order: helper lane/resource lifetime fence -> entry operation gate -> stable operation gate -> original account lease -> stable mutex -> entry mutex. Metadata-only entry operations may use account lease -> entry mutex after releasing source-info gate. Never hold entry mutex while acquiring stable/account gates, or hold an outer account lease while invoking a public stable method. The latter deadlocks against existing stable operations that own their gate while waiting for an account lease. No Argon work runs under an account lease or either store mutex.

Before every next proof, check cancellation and original authorization; join an in-progress source verifier before returning. Registry methods are currently not interruptible inside Argon; that one bounded verification is the documented cancellation latency, not eight parallel hashes. Callback/source success after a reset cannot publish under a replacement session. A source count/checkpoint/roster revision below a retained high water is corruption; greater values may update observation metadata, never silently change saved selections. Unconsumed IDs fail `entry_sync_required`; the helper may offer/schedule separate stable catch-up, but never automatically applies an old intent after it.

## 5. Core API and exact transitions

Proposed Go signatures (clock/random/write/checkpoint seams remain private tests only):

```
Create(ctx, path, pin, source *gymstable.Store) (*Store, error)
Open(ctx, path, expectedPin, source *gymstable.Store) (*Store, error)
Close() error
Upcoming(ctx, session) (EventStatus, error)
Status(ctx, session, saturday string) (EventStatus, error)
History(ctx, session, afterEventID string, limit uint32) (HistoryPage, error)
Receipt(ctx, session, operationID string) (Receipt, error)
Check(ctx, session, saturday string) (CheckResult, error)
Prepare(ctx, session, request Request) (Intent, error)
Apply(ctx, session, operationID string) (MutationResult, error)
Operation(ctx, session, operationID string) (OperationResult, error)
Pending(ctx, session) (OperationResult, error)
Abandon(ctx, session, operationID string) (OperationResult, error)
```

`ctx` is nonnil, mandatory and honored by gate acquisition and publication. Parameter types follow the declared DTOs; path is an absolute clean string. Add strict Parse/Marshal/Validate functions for Pin, Request, Event, Intent, Operation, Receipt and the public response DTOs, plus CalendarID/RulesID/NamespaceID/EventForDate/StoreID/EntryID/ReceiptDigest helpers. Structural parsing never constitutes trusted assignment or import. There is no seed/Lock/Activate method.

**Prepare:** authenticate EntryManage; validate bounded request and exact event; observe clock. If the one pending row has identical request+original generation/view, return the original Intent after final authorization, even if the source advanced or cutoff passed; this is pending-outcome recovery, not new eligibility or Apply permission. Any other pending row returns `entry_pending`. For a new row, require `now < cutoff`, current per-event revision equals ExpectedRevision, operation capacity, event capacity if new, and source identity/high-water coherence. A new replace records the syntactically bounded expected roster revision and selected IDs as **unvalidated intended selection**; their source/roster/class/retirement checks occur only at Apply. Preparation is never displayed as a saved/eligible entry. No new cheap roster callback or Argon is needed for Prepare. After random ID generation and complete bounded shape/capacity preflight, reacquire the original EntryManage lease, recheck the exact pending/CAS state, and take a fresh final clock sample immediately before the preparation batch. Require that final sample strictly before cutoff; equality or crossing while generating the ID fails entry_closed and persists only clock/closure observation. A first event row (revision0) and prepared operation/reservation are synced in one batch. Generate the ID only internally; after unknown Prepare reply, query Pending before retrying. A same-request replay never changes prepared time or operation count. Unknown Prepare ACK recovery checks Pending under the current response view, then matches the *original* intent view/generation and full Request. A new view can inspect or explicitly abandon it, never apply it. If Pending is absent, that observation is not proof that an earlier dispatch never existed; show current event/history and require a new explicit action before preparing again. No prepare path automatically applies from absent or mismatched evidence.

**Apply replace:** lookup the exact operation; reject wrong original generation/view even for a committed row (new views use read-only Operation/Receipt instead). A committed exact operation returns its original receipt with `replayed=true`, without capacity checks, proof regeneration, fresh roster requirements, cutoff rewriting or new revision. An abandoned row conflicts. For prepared state, read/verify exactly the requested consumed assignments through WithEntrySelection, <=5 serial proofs. Under its final original lease and revision fence, require every member currently rostered and nonretired, classes unique, exact candidate descriptor/source binding and XP0. Lock entry mutex; recheck unchanged Intent/pending ID and ExpectedRevision; reproject using immutable DNA/birth at final entry clock, never browser attributes. Preflight the receipt/batch shape with worst-case integer widths, recheck original authorization, then take the final authority clock sample and require it strictly before cutoff. Reproject at that exact final time and encode the bounded receipt once, with no retry loop; if final retirement/size fails, persist the authenticated clock observation and any necessary event closure, then return a definite precommit error without an entry revision. Observation-only I/O is permitted on rejection; it is never a late Apply. Sync operation terminal receipt, event revision/current-operation link, cleared pending ID and high waters atomically. No node/provider call, Argon or source verification follows that sample; only the bounded five condition projections and canonical batch encoding remain. The timestamp denotes that last authoritative pre-write check; an OS write acknowledgement arriving after noon does not invent a second timestamp or grant new late admissions.

**Apply withdraw:** same operation/original-view/CAS/cutoff rules, but no selected proofs or roster/retirement requirement. Under final EntryManage lease, write a new receipt with empty Members and increment that event revision. Removing roster members or source backlog alone cannot prevent an otherwise authorized withdrawal. Stable source identity must still be the established borrowed source; no foreign store substitution. Withdraw before any prior save is an explicit empty revision. No fee or wallet action occurs.

**Abandon:** a current same-gym EntryManage session may explicitly abandon the one prepared operation, including one created under an old view or after its cutoff. Same abandoned ID returns its original terminal row; committed ID returns its existing committed row and never withdraws it. Unknown ID is NotFound; no absent historical intent is executed. Abandon time is durable, pending cleared in the same batch, event revision/current receipt unchanged. Cancellation of an async task is not abandonment or withdrawal.

**Upcoming:** under current View, source metadata identity and monotone entry clock, derive the earliest supported cutoff strictly after that fresh observation and return its EventStatus. It creates no event/operation row or entry; return entry_calendar if no supported future date exists. Its response date/cutoff is the authority-provided navigation default. Browser wallclock never chooses the initial authoritative event.

**Read/query/reopen:** Operation/Receipt/Pending use current View and exact store pin, permit historical original views, never call Apply and never generate new IDs. Receipt is conditional local authority history, not reverified current roster eligibility. Check uses <=5 proofs and one current as-of; it leaves saved history untouched. Status/History are cheap metadata operations with no Argon. At cutoff, queries may still return historical success and original receipts, while fresh mutation fails `entry_closed`.

## 6. Clock and cutoff persistence

Use only the authority's UTC `time.Now().UnixMilli()` with private deterministic test seam. Persist monotone ClockMS on authenticated observations, including failed proof/revision/retirement/cutoff attempts; preserve the newest observed time after a slow source operation even when it fails. Clock rollback below process-seen or persisted high water is `entry_clock`; never clamp a rolled-back clock forward and pretend it is fresh. Entry timestamps must be >= source as-of and immutable born/accepted times.

The final durable mutation guard is authoritative: a prepared-before-noon operation finishing validation at/after noon cannot commit a new save/replace/withdraw. No grace interval, timeout resurrection or client-provided timestamp. `now == cutoff` is closed. Historical replay remains historical success; it cannot renew the entry or alter time. Observation must not scan every historic event: close the specifically queried/mutated row; History closes at most its eight returned rows in one bounded metadata batch. Any future query derives closure from cutoff even if the app was offline.

Event row phase is monotone `accepting -> closed_pending_lock`. `closed_observed_at_ms` records the first successfully synced observation at/after cutoff, not a claim that a daemon wrote at noon. The effective closure is always the Event's exact cutoff. An offline/restarted app cannot extend it. Closed observation/clock writes use already reserved row space and do not consume new operation/event capacity. A prepared intent remains queryable and abandonable after closure but can never create a new committed change. No automatic withdrawal, roster reservation, snapshot lock, seed fallback, expiry deletion or history pruning occurs.

Every uncertain DB write poisons that handle, returns `outcome_unknown`, and requires explicit close/reopen+query. If a batch committed and cancellation, final wrapper failure or lost transport reply follows, report unknown rather than definite cancellation. Precommit cancellation leaves no new entry revision. Cross-DB source observation and entry commits are not advertised as atomic: a source clock/count can advance alone; entry state cannot commit without the final source/account fence. Existing source clocks and assignment/roster history are never rolled back to reconcile an entry failure.

## 7. Disk layout, quotas, audit and recovery

New child directory `gyms/<account_id>/entries`, mode0700, marker `SLUG-CANDIDATE-ENTRIES.json`, mode0600, LevelDB `db/`. Marker ordered fields: `application="slug-candidate-entries", version=1, store_id, pin`, canonicalJSON+LF. Existing markers are not trust discovery: constructors receive expected Pin from the validated parent/source. Reject symlinks/special files and oversized marker bytes before allocation; compare Lstat/opened-fd Stat/SameFile and use bounded reads. Do not recursively create caller paths, adopt an unknown directory, delete partial evidence or recreate a missing established component.

Only LevelDB keys: ASCII `meta`; `e:`+64hex EventID; `o:`+64hex OperationID; `s:`+BE64 operation sequence. `s:` values are exact raw32 OperationID. Reject unknown keys, nested-like malformed encodings, oversized keys/values and counts before copying/unmarshalling. `meta` order: `version,store_id,pin,event_count,operation_count,pending_operation_id,last_operation_id,observed_checkpoint,observed_source_count,observed_roster_revision,clock_ms`. Event-row order: `version,event,entry_id,created_at_ms,revision,latest_operation_id,phase,closed_observed_at_ms`.

Reserve a full 32 KiB terminal Operation slot and full 2 KiB Event slot at Prepare. MaxEvents256 and MaxOperations4096 give a finite logical-record ceiling below136MiB including all fixed-size keys/metadata/marker; this is not a LevelDB physical-disk bound. Prepared->committed/abandoned and accepting->closed never need a fresh count/byte reservation. New prepares fail closed at capacity; receipt lookup, close observation, abandonment and terminal query remain possible. No auto-pruning or replacing old operation IDs. Random collision attempts are bounded before any new durable row.

Open performs a bounded cheap audit, without Argon: exact marker/metadata pin; raw shapes/caps; contiguous operation sequences; unique IDs; exactly one pending row or none; complete operation-state/count/index graph; unique canonical Event rows; generation/view/time/ID consistency; and per-event replay in global operation-sequence order from revision0. Each committed operation must have previousRevision matching the replayed prior event revision, revision+1, action/cardinality/class/slot invariants and immutable request/event equality. Regenerate canonical DNA/manifest class from each retained Assignment.WorkHash and compiled DescriptorID using the existing pure generators; recompute Condition from that DNA, exact birth/save time and XP0. These SHA256-based public derivations are not Argon/proof verification, and cannot authenticate wholesale self-consistent source rewrites. Latest event reference and revision equal the last committed receipt; abandoned/prepared operations cannot change them. All semantic timestamps <=ClockMS, event creation/Prepare before cutoff, committed time before cutoff, closure observed at/after cutoff. Receipt condition arithmetic and Member Assignment structural invariants are recomputed without pretending this is Argon verification. Full current-source proof checks happen only in bounded Check/Apply; wholesale coherent local-authority history replacement is outside this unsigned local journal's authentication claim.

Source identity must equal the expected actual borrowed stable identity. Persist and reject regressions of observed source count/checkpoint/roster revision. Ordinary greater source revisions produce revalidation warnings, not automatic selection changes. Missing/corrupt rows fail closed. Create syncs marker, initial metadata, DB and parent directories before success; Close cancels, joins the real in-flight operation and closes only the owned entry DB. Constructor failure owns partial-resource cleanup and returns nil; callers must transfer interface ownership only on successful construction, preserving the set42 typed-nil repair.

## 8. Additive same-app installation

Keep the current Candidate Pilot bundle, window, Mode, wallet, stable and preview commands. Add no new demo application or production route. Preserve `NewStable` / `--candidate-stable` as the version2 route; add `accountpilot.NewEntries` and an explicit `--candidate-entries` helper/native flag requiring both existing candidate flags. Ordinary defaults remain false. Only the Candidate Pilot build script sets a new private link-time `entryBuild=1` alongside existing candidateBuild/stableBuild; it still opens `/stable.html`. `LaunchEntries` explicitly selects the new helper route. Entry methods on an old route return entry_unavailable without touching storage. New child construction opts into version3 root validation privately; the old child route does not broadly accept unknown marker versions. Account-root marker becomes an explicit **version3** shape containing all existing version2 identity/stable fields byte-equivalent as values, then `entry_schema=1, entry_calendar_id, entry_rules_id, entry_installs`. Each sorted <=2 entry install is `{account_id,pin,phase}` with phase `prepared|ready`. A source child must already have a complete ready stable install before entry preparation; existing interrupted v1/v2 transitions finish only through their previously supported, validated path.

Validate the entire existing v2 root and all established children without logical mutation under the existing instance lock before writing v3. Existing LevelDB/wallet validators may maintain their own lock/log metadata; this is not an assertion that every filesystem byte stays unchanged. No wallet unlock, new account, receipt migration, source rehash or chain initialization is part of that validation. Write v3 with no entry installs durably, then for the logged-in gym persist exact prepared Pin, create/close/sync the empty entry component, persist ready, and only then attach it to the lane. A durable prepared latch permits only absent/completely empty intended component creation or reopening an exactly valid empty initialized component; retain/refuse unknown or partially invalid contents. Ready+missing/corrupt never regenerates. Complete component plus lost ready ACK resumes exactly. No imported entry JSON can satisfy installation.

New code must parse v3 explicitly at every old strict root-marker reader it still invokes (parent and child installPhase), preserving all v2 rules. Old binaries must refuse v3 instead of dropping its fields or rewriting it to v2. The old non-stable manifest route remains incompatible with upgraded roots. TestPoW refusal occurs before directories/marker upgrade. This is a finite additive component upgrade, not a migration of account authority, stable, source registry, wallet, outbox or preview data. Session generation and current view are never installation identity.

Existing lifetime seam: `StableController.openPair/closePair` and Stop's retained read-only reopening must become a triplet: manifest source -> stable -> entry open; entry -> stable -> owned source close, always under laneGate and never under parent/account/controller mutex. No entry handle retains a stable pointer after rebind. Stop cancels/joins active entry proof/task and leaves only the validated stopped metadata handles required for queries; Close joins loop/start/task handles and closes all owned stores. Logout/reset invalidates view first, then cancels/joins outside account leases. Preserve source observer and preview cache boundaries.

## 9. Helper/native protocol proposal

Use separately typed EntryRequest/EntryResponse/EntrySnapshot/EntryJob; do not widen old StableJob/PreviewJob discriminators or reuse an old decoder. All commands stay on the existing serialized native helper channel and shared single work lane. There remains at most one active and one published queued task across stable, preview and entry work. A submitted entry command does not start mining; automatic sync can yield at existing safe cycle boundaries, never within a held account/store lock.

Commands and native `main.Gym` methods:

| Command | Native method | Parameters beyond transport ID |
|---|---|---|
| `entry_snapshot` | `EntrySnapshot()` | none; cheap current-view/lane metadata |
| `entry_upcoming` | `EntryUpcoming(viewID)` | exact view; authority-clock navigation, no event allocation |
| `entry_status` | `EntryStatus(viewID,saturday)` | exact view and date; cheap core status |
| `entry_history` | `EntryHistory(viewID,afterEventID,limit)` | <=8 metadata rows |
| `entry_prepare` | `BeginEntryPrepare(viewID,request)` | exact typed Request |
| `entry_apply` | `BeginEntryApply(viewID,operationID)` | existing intent ID |
| `entry_check` | `BeginEntryCheck(viewID,saturday)` | current saved entry only |
| `entry_job` | `EntryJob(viewID,jobID)` | exact job |
| `entry_cancel` | `CancelEntryJob(viewID,jobID)` | cancel task, not intent |
| `entry_operation` | `EntryOperation(viewID,operationID)` | read only |
| `entry_pending` | `EntryPending(viewID)` | read only |
| `entry_abandon` | `AbandonEntryOperation(viewID,operationID)` | explicit terminal abandonment |

EntryRequest exact order: `id,command,view_id,saturday,after_event_id,limit,request,operation_id,job_id`. Unused scalar fields are empty/zero, Request null unless `entry_prepare`. ID is 1..MaxSafeInteger. EntryResponse order: `id,ok,view,store_id,snapshot,status,history,job,operation,error`; exactly the command-appropriate success pointer is nonnull, all others null, error empty. Failures have view null, store_id empty, all payload pointers null and one allowlisted fixed error. Successful authorized responses carry the **current full** ManifestViewPin and current Entry StoreID in this common envelope, including queries of historical operations; the original Intent/Receipt view remains unchanged inside historical data. The sole success exception is an unavailable Snapshot: common view=null/store_id empty and the exact blank snapshot. Snapshot/Job embedded views and StoreIDs must equal their envelope. Native first requires an authenticated same-view StableSnapshot with its complete validated Pin and StoreID, derives expected entry Pin/StoreID from compiled calendar/rules and the account-authority namespace, and rejects any bare Entry StoreID as discovery/trust. No raw error strings cross the helper/native boundary.

EntrySnapshot order: `version,state,error,view,store_id,pending_operation_id,active_job_id,queued_job_id,last_job_id`. State `idle|busy|failed|unavailable`; unavailable has view null, empty IDs, and only a fixed error or empty string. It contains no saved selection or current eligibility. Every nonblank response is captured/published under the original same-view lease. Snapshot and Job polls read only owned immutable caches. Explicit Status/History/Operation/Pending/Abandon metadata calls must first take a nonblocking/250ms try-lane lifetime fence, then invoke their core method outside all controller/account locks; if the lane is occupied they return busy. They never call registry.Info. All source verification, source.Info refresh and ordinary stable Status acquisition runs inside asynchronous tasks. An already issued synchronous disk write is joined even on timeout; no fake cancellation guarantee is made.

EntrySnapshot active/queued IDs expose only entry-family jobs; last ID is only its retained entry terminal job. Its state is busy when **any** family occupies the global lane, even if both entry IDs are empty. Existing StableSnapshot and PreviewSnapshot likewise expose only their own families. Every current preview==nil discriminator in task selection/snapshot/expiry/cancel/poll must become an explicit family branch without changing old wire DTOs.

EntryJob order: `version,job_id,kind,state,view,store_id,event_id,saturday,operation_id,error,intent,mutation,check`. Kind `prepare|apply|check`; state `queued|running|complete|failed|cancelled`. Exactly one of intent/mutation/check is nonnull for a complete corresponding kind, all null otherwise. Prepare's operationID is empty until its durable Intent is known; apply binds the original operationID at ACK. All jobs bind exact event/date, store and full ManifestViewPin; native retains at most three bounded correlation tuples so terminal polling/cancellation cannot swap parameters. For apply, native resolves metadata from the exact existing Operation before dispatch, never accepts an unrelated job's terminal payload. That preliminary exchange uses a private already-gate-held request function, never recursively calls the public EntryRequest while owning the native pipe gate. Failure before Apply dispatch is definite; loss after possible dispatch is unknown. First checked terminal payload becomes immutable by a bounded canonical digest; later polling/cancellation may not rewrite its Intent, Receipt or Check as-of/status even with identical job/event/operation IDs. Prepare ACK lost before known opID is recovered using Pending and exact request comparison; it never blindly makes another selection.

Fixed error vocabulary: `invalid_request,unauthorized,forbidden,stale_view,busy,entry_unavailable,entry_corrupt,entry_capacity,entry_clock,entry_calendar,entry_closed,entry_conflict,entry_pending,entry_not_found,entry_sync_required,entry_not_rostered,entry_retired,entry_class_conflict,entry_cancelled,outcome_unknown`. Unknown/closed/poisoned source failures map conservatively to unavailable/corrupt; proof failures are never a cue to accept cached claimant data. Any possibly dispatched Prepare/Apply/Abandon whose reply is missing, malformed, uncorrelated or superseded by authorization loss returns `outcome_unknown`, retaining the concrete operation or Pending reconciliation route. Unauthorized/stale responses clear cached full view/pin and old UI task correlation. No rejected promise silently loses unknown-outcome information.

New helper request bound8KiB, response128KiB, existing scanner maximum256KiB unchanged. Preallocation lexical/schema checks bound objects/depth/arrays before JSON unmarshal; nested existing Condition/Item validation remains exact. Public cache strips private Item receipts. Reserve at most 128 KiB for entry terminal/result data **inside the existing aggregate 1 MiB budget**; selected stable page, manifest cards, preview replay and images still share that budget. One accepted new Begin discards the prior entry terminal result; failed/unpublished enqueue preserves it. Retain at most one entry terminal result and one selected metadata page, with their exact canonical bytes plus reservations <=128KiB. Reserve the maximum terminal space before publishing ACK; final lease/queue publication failure rolls back the exact unpublished task and reservation. All existing admission/render/export/stable/preview cache-admission paths must reciprocally charge retained+reserved entry bytes, not merely Entry Begin. Cache pressure returns capacity or evicts only already-discardable terminal presentation; never discard an unresolved durable intent or the fixed selected page. Polls/native parsing/DOM rendering do no Argon, simulation or SVG regeneration. Selected fighters can use existing verified card summaries; this slice adds no new portrait wire command.

## 10. Player flow and preservation

Add “Saturday entry” within the existing stable app. Show selected Saturday, exact noon-Pacific cutoff plus authoritative UTC metadata, saved revision, up to five explicit class-labelled selections, and Save/Replace/Withdraw/Check/History controls. Distinguish draft selection, durable prepared intent, saved entry and `closed_pending_lock`. Suggested plain copy: “Saved entry”, “Entry intake is closed. Event locking is not available in this candidate build”, and “Your roster changed. Check this saved entry again.” No “booked”, “confirmed opponent”, guaranteed Saturday bout or ownership transfer claim.

Clicking Save/Replace may perform Prepare then Apply as one explicit user intent after its exact Intent arrives under the same captured view/event/selection epoch. A lost reply stops automatic application and enters query-first reconciliation. A changed selection/date/view cancels only presentation/task intent; it cannot silently abandon or apply an already durable operation. Unknown Apply/Abandon ACK offers exact Operation query. New-view pending intent is displayed as unresolved; explicit Abandon is required before a new selection, not execution under the new view. A committed historical operation is displayed without replaying mutation.

Roster changes, source append, aging and calendar rollover never silently withdraw, replace, lock, move or hide a saved entry. Check is read-only except observation metadata and warns about off-roster/retired members. Preserve live cards, fixed-page protection, Follow Recent, roster CAS, preview selection/playback, recovery/export holds, Start/Stop and logout semantics. One serialized frontend scheduler gives controls priority and pauses during native modal dialogs. Stale job/response/view epochs cannot repaint the active gym or restore old selections. Use DOM text/image APIs, no arbitrary markup. DOM/keyboard/error-state tests are engineering evidence; actual GUI, accessibility and joint D74 review remain pending.

## 11. Acceptance and independent evidence

No runtime/oracle output is authorized until this exact contract and the remaining engineering precision points below are reviewed. Then independent calendar/preimage/canonical/state vectors must freeze before implementation is compared with them. Never derive expectations from Go output.

- Calendar: canonical leap dates, invalid/day/year bounds, multiple ordinary Saturdays in standard/daylight periods, Saturdays before/after both DST transitions, exact cutoff-1/equality/+1, year rollover, earliest/latest supported date, UTC/local round-trip, `TZ`/host tzdata variation, pinned-byte corruption. Include independently derived 167/168/169-hour consecutive-Saturday cutoff differences as applicable; no assumed constant7×24h UTC interval. Boundary tests use a private clock, not an actual Saturday claim.
- Selection: zero/one/five/six, duplicate IDs/classes, all five current class spellings, different-gym proof, unconsumed ID, source-record digest drift, wrong descriptor, off-roster, exact retirement boundary, both fixtures and held current sessions. Full proof counts <=5 per Apply/Check; no proofs on cheap metadata/polling; cancellation joins an in-progress verifier and starts no next one.
- Ordering: roster mutation before/after proof and final lease; reset/logout and same-generation relogin; source handle rebind while stopped/mining; callback reentry/async misuse; final clock passes cutoff during proof/encoding; rollback after rejected verification. Tests must force the final sample, not merely prepare-time denial.
- Durable state: event/operation capacities at limits with terminal completion reserved; contiguous audit graph, foreign/oversized/missing rows, contradictory revisions, source high-water regression, receipt condition/time corruption; no whole-history Argon on Open. Query/replay after cutoff and date rollover preserve exact bytes and timestamps. Prepared cutoff operations can query/abandon but never commit.
- Crash: actual child-process termination before/after initial marker/meta sync, parent-v3 write, entry prepared/create/ready, entry Prepare batch, Apply batch, closure observation and Abandon; committed-write-error/lost ACK poison+reopen. Unknown partial installation retained/refused; ready missing never recreated. Compare old source/wallet/outbox/stable identities and logical contents, not transient database lock/log bytes.
- Same bundle: both fixture accounts, explicit roster selections/save/replace/withdraw, five/class caps, stop/reopen/history, wrong-account refusal, old-view unknown reconciliation, held edits with existing export refusal, and no seed/result/XP effects. Actual packaged helper uses normal PoW for its source receipts and verifies every displayed Check item independently. Artificial clock tests are separately labelled; no public mining, real keys or official event is used.
- Compatibility: old stable/preview/candidate commands and normal PoW source fixtures retain bytes, D65/condition/engine unchanged, cheap profile refuses before writes, old binary rejects v3, no old root silently adopts new files. Source-hashed normal/race/tagged/codec-fuzz/DOM gates and owned-process/listener cleanup precede packaging.

## 12. Genuine policy gaps and deferred authority

Two existing gaps block **locking**, not reversible intake: (1) whether roster/retirement eligibility freezes at noon, reserves slots, or changes until the bout, including retirement between noon and evening; (2) the exact noon-lock commitment/unknown future-block selector, publication ordering, idle-chain/reorg/outage conflict behavior and cancellation/rescheduling promise. This contract intentionally chooses none of those alternatives. A saved receipt is eligibility-at-save evidence and an intent for later revalidation. `closed_pending_lock` must not be mistaken for any resolved lock policy.

Official distributed event authority, real accounts/portable ownership, permanent genesis and version activation, public signed publication/finality, matching priority, title rules and results/XP/training still need their own implementations and acceptance. Source code access does not settle those promises. No new question to Mike is required to review this intake engineering contract; prepare concrete lock options/evidence before a later product choice is needed.

Source inspection fixed the class enum and removed an unnecessary prepare-time eligibility claim; all actual selection fencing occurs at Apply. Appendices A–C supply the concrete interfaces, cap derivations and complete root reader/writer inventory. Independent review may still identify defects; resolve those from code without weakening player rules or introducing a new user approval request. Pin the reviewed document, TZif input and source snapshot before oracle/runtime authoring.

## Appendix A. Exact types, exported surfaces and edge returns

The ordered shapes in §3 and §9 also define their Go struct declarations/JSON tags: Version and Slot are uint32; Sequence, OperationSequence, all revisions/checkpoints/counts carried in public results, Generation and transport ID are uint64; Limit and stored EventCount/OperationCount are uint32; every `*_ms` is int64; flags are bool; IDs/date/action/state/error/phase/class/eligibility are string. Collections are slices of their named DTO (not interfaces/maps), except the existing nested types retain their existing Go definitions. `Request.ProspectIDs` and `EventStatus.SavedIDs` are []string. `Pin.StablePin` is gymstable.Pin; Member.Assignment is gymstable.Assignment; Member.ConditionAtSave is fightercondition.Snapshot; CheckMember.Item is gymstable.Item with its private receipt cleared. `Operation.Receipt` is *Receipt; `OperationResult.Operation` is *Operation. Event/Request/Intent/Receipt/Status nested values are values, not nullable pointers. EntryResponse payloads and View are pointers; EntryJob.Intent/Mutation/Check and EntrySnapshot.View are pointers. Unused pointers must be null, not omitted. The existing ManifestViewPin, Manifest, DNA, Assignment and Condition field order is unchanged.

Exact core signatures (with the already defined package types):

```go
func Create(ctx context.Context, path string, pin Pin, source *gymstable.Store) (*Store, error)
func Open(ctx context.Context, path string, expected Pin, source *gymstable.Store) (*Store, error)
func (s *Store) Close() error
func (s *Store) Upcoming(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session) (EventStatus, error)
func (s *Store) Status(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (EventStatus, error)
func (s *Store) History(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, afterEventID string, limit uint32) (HistoryPage, error)
func (s *Store) Receipt(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, operationID string) (Receipt, error)
func (s *Store) Check(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, saturday string) (CheckResult, error)
func (s *Store) Prepare(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, request Request) (Intent, error)
func (s *Store) Apply(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, operationID string) (MutationResult, error)
func (s *Store) Operation(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, operationID string) (OperationResult, error)
func (s *Store) Pending(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session) (OperationResult, error)
func (s *Store) Abandon(ctx context.Context, session gymstable.Session, operationID string) (OperationResult, error)
```

For each T in Pin/Request/Event/Intent/Operation/Receipt/EventStatus/CheckResult/HistoryPage/MutationResult/OperationResult: `ParseT(raw []byte) (T,error)`, `MarshalT(value T) ([]byte,error)`, `ValidateT(value T) (T,error)`. Validation produces owned values and does not acquire authority. Cross-object Pin/Event/receipt relationships are additionally checked at trusted API boundaries. `CalendarID() string`, `RulesID() string`, `NamespaceID(network uint32, genesis, accountAuthorityID string) (string,error)`, `ID(pin Pin) (string,error)`, `EventForDate(pin Pin,saturday string) (Event,error)`, `EntryID(storeID,eventID,gymID string) (string,error)`, `ReceiptDigest(receipt Receipt) (string,error)`. Calendar ID/rules constants resolve only this compiled candidate version; namespace/Pin validation binds the normal-profile fixture chain.

Exact new gymstable shapes/methods:

```go
// Ordered JSON fields use the corresponding snake_case spelling.
type EntrySourceInfo struct {
    Version uint32
    StoreID string
    Pin Pin
    Checkpoint uint64
    ObservedSourceCount uint64
    RosterRevision uint64
}
type EntrySelectionMember struct { Slot uint32; Item Item }
type EntrySelection struct { Version uint32; Status Status; AsOfMS int64; Members []EntrySelectionMember }
func (s *Store) EntrySourceInfo(ctx context.Context) (EntrySourceInfo, error)
func (s *Store) ReadEntrySelection(ctx context.Context, session Session, ids []string) (EntrySelection, error)
func (s *Store) WithEntrySelection(ctx context.Context, session Session, expectedRosterRevision uint64, ids []string, fn func(EntrySelection, func() error) error) error
```

These selection methods require 1..5 canonical unique sorted IDs. No public function accepts an EntrySelection as authoritative input. The callback is synchronous trusted composition, not a caller receipt factory. Private full source records are removed before exposing Item values. Empty Check/withdraw paths bypass selection proofs and use the appropriate final original account lease. Existing stable writes/count observations keep their current semantics; no roster/checkpoint/operation mutation is introduced by selection.

Routine edge returns: History limit is exactly1..8; unknown nonempty retained cursor is entry_not_found; a valid last cursor yields empty events/next_event_id empty/has_more false. `next_event_id` is the last returned row ID only when another retained row follows; otherwise empty. Check of a nonexistent valid Event or an empty prepared/withdrawn selection returns empty Members, current EventStatus, observed as-of and current roster revision; it does not allocate an Event. Receipt of a prepared/abandoned operation returns entry_not_found (Operation still returns its state); unknown operation does too. Upcoming outside the supported future-cutoff range returns entry_calendar. A nonexistent past Status is closed_pending_lock with exists=false/closed_observed_at_ms=0 and no event-row allocation. A prepared event with no committed selection has revision0 and an empty Check.

Constructor/route interfaces: `accountpilot.NewEntries(config pilot.Config) (*StableController,error)` and `pilot.NewEntryManifestAccount(config Config, account StableAccountConfig) (*StableController,error)` explicitly select entry-enabled behavior; existing constructors remain old routes. `bridge.LaunchEntries(helper,dataDir,node string) (*StableBridge,error)` selects all three candidate flags; `(*StableBridge).EntryRequest(ctx context.Context, request pilot.EntryRequest) pilot.EntryResponse` returns the typed error envelope, including unknown outcomes. `(*Gym)` native methods in §9 all return pilot.EntryResponse and take exactly the listed strings, typed gymentry.Request, uint64 revisions/cursors only where named, and uint32 limit. They expose no generic body, path, token, seed, clock or source-selector field.

Add `pilot.EntryControllerAPI` extending the existing StableControllerAPI and PreviewControllerAPI, with EntrySnapshot() EntrySnapshot; EntryUpcoming/EntryStatus/EntryHistory returning their core DTO,error; BeginEntryPrepare/Apply/Check returning EntryJob,error; EntryJob/CancelEntryJob returning EntryJob,error; EntryOperation/EntryPending/AbandonEntryOperation returning gymentry.OperationResult,error. Each non-Snapshot method takes context.Context then the exact view string and remaining §9 arguments. Both parent and entry-enabled child implement this interface; parent wrapper captures the original child/view and never replaces a session. New `ServeEntries(ctx, controller, input io.Reader, output io.Writer) error` dispatches the three preserved existing closed protocol families plus this separately parsed family. Old ServeStable/ServePreview paths do not gain entry authority merely by recognizing method names.

Command field correlation is exact: snapshot has all non-ID/command fields empty; upcoming/pending require only View; status/check require View+Saturday; history requires View+Limit and optional AfterEventID; prepare requires View+nonnull Request only; apply/operation/abandon require View+OperationID only; job/cancel require View+JobID only. Every unused scalar is empty/zero and Request null. Core Request carries its own EventID/date/CAS; native must not mix those with stale top-level dates. Successful Pending alone may carry OperationResult.operation=null; Operation and Abandon never do. The common response View/StoreID identifies the current query, while stored operation View/Generation remain historical.

Metadata responses additionally match request ID, current full View, expected derived StoreID, requested date/EventID, operation ID or history cursor/limit. Upcoming's cutoff must be strictly after its observed_at_ms and recompute as the earliest supported one. A terminal job can be accepted only from its retained original request tuple, or from an exact same-view Snapshot-discovered job followed by a checked job fetch that establishes the complete tuple before actions. The latter never authorizes auto-Apply. At most three native correlation tuples and one terminal payload digest are retained, all cleared on accepted new relevant Begin/view loss/helper failure. Unpublished ACK failure cancels/removes only that exact task and releases its cache reservation. Missing/malformed Prepare reply -> Pending query; same-request matching under a new view is read-only, not a mutation authorization.

## Appendix B. Conservative maximum shapes (no generated expected outputs)

These are source-type bounds, not simulation, oracle or runtime output. Existing gymstable.MaxAssignmentSize=2048 and MaxItemSize=8192 are retained. For the closed Condition snapshot, fixed fields/ASCII selectors, exact bounded integers, two five-attribute objects and no arrays give a conservative1536-byte bound; all non-ID strings come from existing compiled enums/selectors. One Member is at most2048+1536+128=3712 bytes, below its4096 limit. A five-member Receipt fits5×4096+2048=22,528 bytes. Even charging the complete8KiB Request cap plus1024 bytes of Intent wrapping, plus512 bytes of Operation wrapping, its terminal row bound is22,528+8192+1024+512=32,256 bytes <32,768. No maximum-length arbitrary string enters these structures.

Event's seven fixed fields fit1024 bytes; Event row fits1024+480=1504<2048. EventStatus's fixed fields and five64-hex IDs fit4096; History at8 rows fits8×4096+1024=33,792. A CheckMember fits8192+128=8320<10,240; CheckResult fits5×10,240+4096+512=55,808; adding8192 for the complete native/helper View/job/envelope gives64,000<131,072. Max object depth including envelope/job/check/member/item/manifest/DNA/attributes is8 (the declared cap10 leaves bounded envelope room); arrays remain path/count restricted. A complete parent v3 marker fits two existing stable Pins and two entry Pins: each existing Pin is conservatively <=1536, each Entry Pin <=2048, both install wrappers together <=512 and root fields <=512, giving2×1536+2×2048+512+512=8192. Because equality leaves no LF headroom, **v3 marker limit is16KiB**, explicitly new-version-only; old v1/v2 limits remain8KiB. No runtime-general unbounded-marker change follows.

Max retained operation values4096×32,768=134,217,728 bytes; event values256×2048=524,288; bounded keys/indexes/marker/meta stay below an additional1MiB. Thus136MiB is a conservative total logical-value/key allowance, excluding LevelDB/WAL/compaction overhead. Each reservation guarantees terminal row space independently of later event/operation count saturation. Implementation tests must assert typed/canonical shape bounds and reject any structure exceeding them; discovering a mistake requires reviewed correction before new expected outputs, not a hidden fallback.

## Appendix C. Complete root/lifetime footprint

The new route must inventory **readers and writers**, not just teach one parser version3:

- `desktop/accountpilot/manifest_files.go`: old v1 reader/open remains unchanged and refuses3.
- `desktop/accountpilot/stable_files.go`: old readStableMarker/openStableAccountStore and StableController.install remain v2 behavior on the old route. New entry route uses a closed v3 reader/writer and feature-selected private common initialization/validation, under the same already-held root instance lock; it cannot call a second public constructor and reacquire that lock.
- Parent stable installation has both absent->prepared and prepared->ready marker writes. On the new route they **must preserve every v3 calendar/rules/entry-install field**. Never pass a v3 marker through old writeStableMarker and truncate it.
- `desktop/pilot/stable_install.go`: installPhase, used by CreateStableComponent and AttachStable, accepts3 only on the privately entry-enabled constructor path, validates the full3 shape, and obtains the same stable installation Pin/phase. Entry-specific CreateEntryComponent/AttachEntries validate the entry latch separately. Old constructors still refuse3.
- `desktop/pilot/stable_controller.go` openPair/closePair and Stop/read-only reopen acquire/release the triplet in dependency order under laneGate; source lifecycle may not leave entry borrowing the previous closed stable pointer.
- `desktop/accountpilot/manifest_controller.go` withCapability extends only the signed_in/nonbusy requirement to EntryManage and preserves successful-construction-only cleanup ownership.
- `gymaccount/types.go` capability constant and `sessions.go` validCapability add EntryManage; heldCapability remains exactly its enumerated prior restrictions. Enrollment/noRecoveryRequired/mining-token checks remain intact.
- `desktop/cmd/slugpilot/main.go`, native main/bridge and build script select the explicit new route/flag/default above. `desktop/candidate_path.go` keeps its existing protected-root/marker-presence checks; do not generically relax path validation because a new marker version exists.

Finite initialization cases: fresh entry-enabled root creates the ordinary account authority/gyms directory and v3 root with both install arrays empty; no fighters/entries/mining are created. A populated v2 upgrade validates the full old root/children and retains all existing stable install values, including prepared entries, in one durable v3 promotion. A supported v1 root can use the existing logically read-only old-child validation and move through the explicit v2-compatible stable preparation values inside the private upgrade path; no unknown partial child is adopted. At login, first finish that gym's preexisting wallet/enrollment and stable prepared->ready contract, using the v3-preserving writer; only after stable ready may entry prepared->created->ready run. A v3 root's second fixture may have no stable install yet: add/finish its stable rows while preserving the first gym's stable and entry histories, then initialize only its own entry store. A resumed stable-prepared row is validated against the exact existing stable rules; a ready source is never recreated. Entry initialization handles close before attaching the long-lived triplet. Reset/logout can cancel/join at every stage and cannot convert a missing ready component into a new one.

A root-level upgrade crash test must cover fresh, populated-v2, stable-prepared, entry-prepared/created/ready, and second-fixture first login. Compare authoritative logical source/wallet/roster/entry histories and pins; permitted LevelDB lock/log maintenance is recorded separately. Old v1/v2 callers must refuse a v3 root before a marker rewrite. No source change is authorized by this inventory until the exact revised contract is approved.
